players.product: laser annealing & wet-processing systems for leading-edge nodes

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 revenue was $193 million, above the midpoint of guidance, with non-GAAP operating income of $23 million and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $0.33 - both bottom-line figures exceeding the guidance ranges. Gross margin was 39.5%, operating expenses $53.3 million, tax expense ~$3 million at a ~12% effective rate, and net income approximately $22 million on 67 million shares. By segment: semiconductor revenue $131 million (+20% sequentially, 68% of total) on laser annealing to leading-edge foundry logic and memory customers plus wet processing for advanced packaging; compound semiconductor $21 million (+9%, 11%); data storage $22 million (+117%, 11%); scientific and other flat at $20 million (10%). By region: U.S. 31%, Asia Pacific excluding China 36%, China 25%, EMEA and rest of world 8%.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue $193M; non-GAAP EPS $0.33; gross margin 39.5%; semiconductor $131M (+20% QoQ), compound semi $21M, data storage $22M (+117% QoQ)

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 guidance: revenue $200-220 million, gross margin 41-42%, operating expenses $57-58 million, net income $23-33 million and diluted EPS $0.35-0.49 on 67 million shares. Full-year 2026 guidance was updated to revenue of $780-810 million (raised by about $25 million), gross margin 40-42%, operating expenses $215-225 million and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $1.36-1.61. Full-year segment expectations: semiconductor revenue to grow more than 10%, compound semiconductor revenue to approximately DOUBLE versus 2025, and data storage revenue to double year over year. In 2027 management expects revenue growth to meaningfully accelerate, particularly in advanced packaging.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 guide $200M-$220M, EPS $0.35-$0.49; FY2026 revenue $780M-$810M, EPS $1.36-$1.61; compound semi and data storage each to double in 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Order momentum accelerated across all major end markets. Veeco secured $200 MILLION IN ADVANCED PACKAGING ORDERS for wet processing and lithography systems during Q2, principally for delivery in 2027, strengthening visibility into that year. Management said a significant portion of anticipated 2027 revenue is already represented in backlog, that visibility into 2027 is much stronger than historical norms at this point in the year, and that customers are sharing long-range forecasts beyond 2027 that they would not normally share. Data storage is booked well into 2027 on HAMR-based production roadmaps. Customer deposits rose $45 million in the quarter to $114 million.
quarterly_data.figure: $200M advanced packaging orders in Q2 (mostly 2027 delivery); customer deposits +$45M to $114M

quarterly_data.signal: Veeco plans to MORE THAN DOUBLE CAPACITY in advanced packaging and silicon photonics during 2027, expanding internal manufacturing on the East Coast plus strategic outsourcing partnerships with contract manufacturers in Southeast Asia, and adding and training personnel. The company is deliberately spending ahead of revenue in the second half of 2026: approximately $10 million of incremental operating expenses and roughly 75 basis points of full-year gross-margin impact from one-time capacity set-up and contract-manufacturer onboarding costs. This is why the full-year revenue guide rose while the EPS guide came down. The revenue ramp from the optical networking, data storage and advanced packaging orders begins slightly at the end of Q4 2026, starts in Q1 2027 and gets more up to speed in Q2 2027, with the majority falling in 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: Capacity in advanced packaging and silicon photonics to more than double during 2027; ~$10M incremental opex and ~75bps gross-margin impact in 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Silicon photonics and indium phosphide lasers are Veeco's clearest AI-linked growth vector, with a projected $700 million SAM by 2030 for its role in InP laser manufacturing and a stated opportunity of AT LEAST $2 BILLION over the coming years across the laser manufacturing flow - epitaxy, wet processing and laser facet coating. Announced with the results: a global leader in optical and photonics technologies selected Veeco's Lumina+ MOCVD system to fabricate indium phosphide lasers for the datacom industry; Lumina+ offers the largest batch size in the MOCVD industry, best-in-class throughput, lowest cost per wafer, and can deposit high-quality epitaxial layers on InP wafers of any size. Veeco is also a market leader in WaferEtch/WaferStorm wet processing and in the SPECTOR ion beam deposition tool used for the critical laser facet coating step, where its IBD is differentiated as the industry moves to higher-power lasers with stricter film specifications. Management framed the driver as the industry 'overcoming the copper wall,' with hyperscalers advancing EML pluggables, silicon photonics pluggables and the longer-term near-package and co-packaged optics architectures - all of which rely increasingly on InP lasers.
quarterly_data.figure: InP laser SAM ~$700M by 2030; total laser-manufacturing opportunity at least $2B; Lumina+ MOCVD selected by a global optical/photonics leader for datacom InP lasers

quarterly_data.signal: Annealing delivered RECORD revenue across both the LSA and NSA product lines in Q2, with a projected annealing SAM of approximately $1.3 billion by 2030. Veeco remains the production tool of record for laser spike annealing at ALL THREE Tier 1 logic/foundry customers. On next-generation nanosecond annealing: a Tier 1 customer successfully completed its evaluation and placed a FOLLOW-ON ORDER for a second system shipping in the second half of 2026, and the third Tier 1 logic customer received an NSA evaluation tool - meaning Veeco has now engaged all three Tier 1 logic customers with NSA technology.
quarterly_data.figure: Record LSA and NSA revenue; annealing SAM ~$1.3B by 2030; production tool of record at all 3 Tier 1 logic customers; NSA follow-on order shipping H2 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Memory is described as a significant long-term growth opportunity as AI compute architectures accelerate DRAM and NAND demand and create new thermal processing and material requirements. Veeco is the production tool of record at A TIER 1 HIGH-BANDWIDTH MEMORY MANUFACTURER that is accelerating its investments in 2026. An LSA evaluation is advancing at a second Tier 1 DRAM customer with potential follow-on orders in the 2027-2028 timeframe, and engagement is expanding with a third DRAM customer that could enter an evaluation agreement over the coming quarters. Several NAND customers are exploring LSA and NSA applications. Separately, multiple IBD300 systems are under evaluation for advanced DRAM applications such as bit line metallization. The memory industry is at the early stages of adopting laser-based annealing.
quarterly_data.figure: Production tool of record at a Tier 1 HBM manufacturer accelerating 2026 investment; LSA evaluation at a second Tier 1 DRAM customer; multiple IBD300 systems in DRAM evaluation

quarterly_data.signal: Advanced packaging is becoming a materially larger part of the business through the wet processing and lithography portfolio, with demand driven by heterogeneous integration and increasingly complex 2.5D and 3D architectures. Veeco projects the advanced packaging SAM will approach $1 BILLION BY 2030 and expects to gain share within it. The company is actively engaged with a Tier 1 foundry on a PANEL PROCESSING opportunity and is encouraged by the progress. Manufacturing footprint is expanding both in-house and with outsourced partners in Southeast Asia to support the growth.
quarterly_data.figure: Advanced packaging SAM approaching $1B by 2030; active panel processing engagement with a Tier 1 foundry

quarterly_data.signal: Veeco remains the leader in ion beam deposition for EUV mask blanks and has extended its ion beam technology to EUV PELLICLES, which protect defect-free masks and improve productivity as EUV utilisation scales. It continues to win production business at a Tier 1 foundry and is engaging new customers for EUV pellicles, and is positioned as the industry advances toward high-NA lithography. Total ion beam deposition SAM is projected at approximately $500 million by 2030, driven by the IBD300 platform for low-resistance metals plus the EUV deposition leadership position.
quarterly_data.figure: IBD SAM ~$500M by 2030; EUV pellicle production wins at a Tier 1 foundry

quarterly_data.signal: Compound semiconductor beyond silicon photonics: GaN power is projected at a $250 million SAM by 2030, supported by AI data center power efficiency, electrification and high-power-density applications. Veeco is progressing with a leading power IDM customer where the Propel 300 platform continues to advance toward production following a previously announced pilot line order, positioning Veeco for future capacity expansions, and it is a member of the imec 300-millimeter GaN Power Consortium. The 'other photonics' category - red microLEDs, low earth orbit satellites and AR/VR - is projected at a $550 million SAM by 2030.
quarterly_data.figure: GaN power SAM ~$250M by 2030; other photonics SAM ~$550M by 2030; Propel 300 advancing to production at a leading power IDM

quarterly_data.signal: Balance sheet and merger status: Veeco ended the quarter with cash and short-term investments of $429 million, up $46 million. Accounts receivable fell $3 million to $148 million, inventory rose $10 million to $292 million and accounts payable fell $3 million to $57 million. Cash flow from operations was $51 million and capital expenditure $4 million. The pending merger with Axcelis continues to progress as planned, with shareholder approval secured from both companies and all regulatory clearances obtained other than China antitrust approval; management continues to target a second-half 2026 closing and did not take questions on the transaction.
quarterly_data.figure: $429M cash and short-term investments (+$46M); Q2 OCF $51M; Axcelis merger targeting H2 2026 close, pending China antitrust
